verdict: All 148 team names in the saved 2026 feeds (116 college, 32 NFL) go to the right school or team in Thursday's setup, and all 136 top-level schools of 2020-25 are reached once I add, from memory, the 21 schools that had no game in the feeds' 7 days. The risk is in spellings the 2020-25 feed may have used that I could not see: some (for example "Miami RedHawks", "Louisiana Monroe Warhawks", "North Carolina State Wolfpack") go to the wrong school even with the team files. Without the team files more fail, including the real 2026 spelling "UMass Minutemen". A wrong name only loses that game's final score and never takes another game's score, but the report logs the loss as "no game", not as a name problem, and it affects profit and loss, the ROI veto and calibration, not CLV. The matching step itself held on every test built from the real schedule, and a names-only check on the probe's saved schedule can confirm the historical spellings on Thursday before any price is opened.

defects.title: The prefix rule sends some plausible Odds API spellings to the wrong school, even with the team files, and the lost game is logged as 'no game'
defects.evidence: outcomes._school resolves 'Miami RedHawks' and 'Miami (Ohio) RedHawks' to Miami; 'Louisiana Monroe Warhawks' to Louisiana; 'North Carolina State Wolfpack' to North Carolina; 'Southern California Trojans' to Southern (Jaguars); 'Texas El Paso Miners' to Texas; 'Nevada Las Vegas Rebels' to Nevada; 'Alabama Birmingham Blazers' to Alabama. Another 14 spellings are unresolved even with raw files (for example 'Mississippi Rebels', 'Albany Great Danes', 'Southeastern Louisiana Lions'). None of the 116 college names in the 2026 feed does this; whether the 2020-25 feed used any of these spellings is unknown. On all real 2020-25 games of those schools, 0 of 993 synthetic events took another game's score (no school in an FBS game plays twice within 36 hours), so the only effect is lost final scores (up to about 70 games per school), counted under cfb_no_game.
defects.smallest_fix: On Thursday, after the probe and before any F1 price is opened, run scratch/scripts/thursday_names_preflight.py on the probe's saved schedule, which holds names only. It runs the engine's own name functions and match() and lists every prefix or unresolved name. Then add the group B aliases (alias_proposal.csv), either only those that actually appear or all of them. Simulated: 0 names made worse, and all 148 feed names unchanged.

defects.title: Without the raw team files the college join silently falls back to the prefix rule alone, and the report does not say which setup ran
defects.evidence: cfb_names returns an empty lookup when REPO/cfb-weather/data/raw/cfbfastr is missing, as in any worktree or cloud checkout. Then the real 2026 spelling 'UMass Minutemen' is unresolved, 'Appalachian State Mountaineers' is unresolved, 'Southern Mississippi Golden Eagles' goes to Southern, 'Houston Baptist Huskies' to Houston and 'Texas A&M-Commerce Lions' to Texas. The preflight test in this worktree printed 'MISSING' and lost 15 of 920 synthetic 2024 games, against 3 with the files. The planned Thursday run in ~/code/value-finder has the files, so it is not affected as planned.
defects.smallest_fix: Run `uv run markets price-engine` only from the live checkout (the F1 cache lives there anyway). Optionally add one report line saying whether the team_info files were found and how many alias keys were built, or add the group A and C aliases.

defects.title: One game listed under two event ids gets its final score twice and is not flagged
defects.evidence: In the preflight test, a synthetic relisted event ('cfb10-relisted') matched the same score-table row as 'cfb10'. engine.entries takes one bet per side per event_id and cmean clusters standard errors by event_id, so a relisted game could be bet and graded twice. The live CFB board already removes relisted events (board.one_row_per_game). Whether F1 has any is unknown.
defects.smallest_fix: The preflight writes one_game_two_events.csv from the probe schedule before any price is opened. If it is empty, nothing is needed; if not, the hub decides before the run.
